items.title: Recognizing Products and Factors

sections.normalized_html: Identify the product and the factors of the equation [MATH: 42 = 2 \times 3 \times 7.]
sections.readable_text: Identify the product and the factors of the equation [MATH: 42 = 2 \times 3 \times 7.]

sections.normalized_html:
The result of a multiplication problem is called the product, while the numbers being multiplied are called the factors.

In this equation,

  • [MATH: 42] is the result (the product), and

  • [MATH: 2,] [MATH: 3,] and [MATH: 7] are the numbers being multiplied (the factors).

Therefore, "the product is [MATH: 42,] while [MATH: 2, 3,] and [MATH: 7] are the factors."

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The result of a multiplication is called a product.

Content:
For example, when we multiply the numbers [MATH: 2] and [MATH: 3], the result is [MATH: 6.] We say that the number [MATH: 6] is the product of [MATH: 2] and [MATH: 3.] The numbers [MATH: 2] and [MATH: 3] are called factors.

Item 2 — Example: Recognizing Products and Factors

[IMG: /graphics/8d0decf176d9b72170a1ee962b7bfc0f]

Therefore, "the product is [MATH: 42,] while [MATH: 2, 3,] and [MATH: 7] are the factors."
